properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. It came from the dev_reflow2 two-agent exercise, 2026-09-28/29 (art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29, items D8, I9, I11 and I12). There a designer agent modelled a new engine whose front door is flo2's EXISTING TypeScript gateway (kept on the owner agent's word), whose callers are outside agents and services, and whose hardware is bought by Anthony. The designer's words: "Expected: a way to mark a component as external or context, not part of this system's spine"; "Expected: `published` to imply outside consumers, or an Actor to count as a consumer". Anthony asked for every idea from the report to be brainstormed (2026-09-29).

WHAT WORKS TODAY, measured 2026-09-29 on 0.74.0 (the three findings beside this node):
- `contains` under the Project clears level_spine_disagreement for an outside part, but nothing then says it is outside.
- CONSUMES from an Actor clears unconsumed_interface, but only through create_edge, because the typed `consumes` refuses a non-Component.
- `governed_by ruling=parks` clears an unmet requirement, but it asserts "correctly unmet", which a requirement a person WILL meet is not.

THE OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) A BOUNDARY MARKER ON COMPONENT: `boundary: ours | outside` (or `context`). An outside part can provide and consume, sits under the Project, is never counted as built or unallocated here, and the hierarchy, single-point-of-failure and build-coverage rules read it. Cheapest: one enum and a few rule reads. Counter: it becomes the easy way to silence a detector by calling an inconvenient part "outside"; and for a part another reflow2 design owns, it is a second way to say what (b) already says.
(b) USE WHAT EXISTS FOR A PART ANOTHER DESIGN OWNS: mirror that design's surface (mirror_surface / pair_designs), and declare our side's contract `designation: required`. flo2's gateway IS in flo2's design, so for this case it is available now. Counter: heavy for a one-line fact, and useless for an outside part with no design (a vendor API, a person, a standard).
(c) OUTSIDE CALLERS ARE ACTORS: the typed `consumes` takes an Actor source, and unconsumed_interface reads `published` (as it already reads `required`), softening to "which outside users rely on it?". Nearly free: the schema already allows it. Counter: an Actor per caller class is modelling nobody asked for; `published` alone may be enough.
(d) A PERSON IS ALLOCATED A REQUIREMENT: an Actor or Contributor is the party that meets it, planned, so the requirement reads "allocated outside the design" rather than parked or unmet. Counter: this is req:vocabulary-covers-personnel's ground ("who performs a function"), which was deferred; a SATISFIES from a person asserts delivery before it happens.
(e) NOTHING NEW: Project containment, an Actor via create_edge, and parking with a sentence of prose. It works today. Counter: every detector and every later reader has to re-derive "outside" from prose. That is the state the three findings measured.

RANKING, as a finding and not a choice: (c) is the smallest change and removes one misfiling outright; (a) removes the other two and carries the silencing risk; (b) is already possible and fits only design-owned parts; (d) waits on the personnel requirement.
properties.name: OPEN — how does a design say that something EXISTS and is NOT OURS: an existing part it relies on (flo2's gateway, in front of a new engine), an outside caller of a published contract, or a person who will meet a requirement? Today each gets misfiled: nested inside the system, left raising "nothing uses this", or parked as if correctly unmet
properties.rationale: Three findings in one report were the same absence seen from three detectors: "outside" has no word. That makes it one question, not three, and it is recorded as one question so the answer cannot be found three different ways.
